summary.headline: Orders slipped 3.6% to 914 but both weekly targets were beaten; the quarter and year remain behind target and returns rose again.

points.what: Orders came in at 914, down 3.6% week on week (34 fewer), yet 77.1% above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Year-on-year growth of 77.1% is above the 75% growth the targets assume, so the week still sits ahead of the weekly target of 889 orders.

points.what: Gross revenue reached $68,099, up 3.3% week on week and 89.4% year on year, above the 8-week average of $63,089.
points.so_what: This was 104.5% of the weekly revenue target of $65,137, a $2,962 surplus for the week.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue stands at $450,760, or 96.8% of the $465,479 target for the same weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter is $14,719 behind target with 6 weeks left and $433,326 still needed to reach the $884,086 full-quarter target.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 27 Apr 2026 was 11.3%, up 1.3 pp week on week and 1.1 pp year on year.
points.so_what: Both moves are assessed as bad and the rise is above the 1.0 pp threshold, making it the main quality watch item this week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate has risen for three consecutive weeks, from 8.7% to 11.3% in the mature week of 27 Apr 2026.
points.so_what: This is a flagged streak in the bad direction, so the level warrants monitoring rather than being read as one-off noise.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate always refers to the mature week of 27 Apr 2026; the two most recent weeks are still immature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week of 11 May is not yet visible, so this measure lags the other KPIs by about two weeks.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 96.8% of target and year-to-date is 94.1%, with every month from January to May (MTD) behind target.
points.so_what: Beating the weekly target does not change the quarter or year position, which both remain behind the 2026 targets.

points.what: Orders hit 102.8% of the weekly target (914 versus 889) and revenue hit 104.5% ($68,099 versus $65,137).
points.so_what: Both weekly measures are ahead of target, and next week's bar rises to 962 orders and $70,820 of revenue.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is $1,166,317, or 94.1% of the $1,240,034 target to date, a shortfall of $73,717.
points.so_what: With 33 weeks left, $2,722,485 is still required to reach the full-year target of $3,888,802.

points.what: The revenue run-rate needed for the rest of the year is $82,500 a week, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $64,014.
points.so_what: At the current pace the full-year target of $3,888,802 remains out of reach, even in a week that beat its weekly target.

points.what: North America orders fell 11.7% to 197, a drop of 26 orders and 76.5% of the total week-on-week change.
points.so_what: North America was the largest single contributor to the decline, while APAC held flat at 402 orders and EMEA rose 2.3% to 181.

points.what: Display orders fell 44.4% to 25, down 20 orders and 58.8% of the total change; Organic fell 9.3% to 137, down 14 orders.
points.so_what: Display and Organic account for most of the week's order decline despite together making up a small share of volume.

points.what: Search, at 70.0% of orders, edged down 1.2% to 640, while Email rose 12.0% to 56 and Facebook rose 3.7% to 56.
points.so_what: The largest source was broadly stable, so the week's decline sits with smaller sources rather than with Search.

points.what: Average order value rose 6.1% week on week to $87.98 and was 5.7% above last year's $83.23.
points.so_what: Higher value per order sits alongside revenue rising 3.3% in a week when orders fell 3.6%.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved to 15.3%, down 0.8 pp week on week and 1.0 pp year on year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $804 of revenue, so the improvement is a modest positive for the week.

points.what: New customer signups rose 21.2% week on week to 252, and were 13.0% above last year.
points.so_what: Signups grew while orders fell 3.6%, so customer acquisition moved in the opposite direction to weekly order volume.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 27 Apr 2026 was 11.3%, versus 10.0% the prior week and 10.2% last year.
points.so_what: Returns are not deducted from gross revenue, so a higher return rate is not reflected in the reported $68,099.

points.so_what: This is the third consecutive move in the bad direction, so order quality warrants attention alongside the revenue strength.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate has risen for three consecutive weeks, from 8.7% to 11.3% in the mature week of 27 Apr 2026.
points.so_what: A sustained rise in returns means a growing share of the week's orders does not stay with the customer, working against gross revenue.

points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week of 11 May is not yet known, so this measure lags the rest of the report by two weeks.

points.so_what: The quarter needs $433,326 of revenue in those 6 weeks to meet the full quarter target of $884,086.

points.what: Orders hit 102.8% of the weekly target (914 versus 889) and revenue 104.5% (68,099 versus 65,137), both ahead.
points.so_what: The bar rises next week, with targets of 962 orders and $70,820 of revenue.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue stands at 96.8% of target and year-to-date at 94.1%, $73,717 below the target to date.
points.so_what: Despite an ahead-of-target week, both the quarter and the year remain behind, with every month from January to May month-to-date behind target.

points.what: Meeting the $3,888,802 full-year target needs $82,500 of revenue a week for the remaining 33 weeks, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $64,014.
points.so_what: At the current pace the full-year target is out of reach, so the size of the required step-up is the key number to track.

points.what: North America orders fell 11.7% to 197, a contribution of -26 orders and 76.5% of the total weekly decline.
points.so_what: North America accounts for most of the week's order decline, even though it is only 21.6% of orders.

points.what: Display orders dropped 44.4% to 25, contributing -20 orders or 58.8% of the change, and Organic fell 9.3% to 137.
points.so_what: Display is the largest single source of the decline despite holding just 2.7% share, so the fall came from smaller sources rather than Search.

points.what: APAC was flat at 402 orders (+0.2%) and EMEA rose 2.3% to 181, while Email orders grew 12.0% to 56.
points.so_what: The largest region held steady, so the week's shortfall was concentrated rather than broad-based, and all regions remain above last year.

points.what: AOV rose 6.1% week on week to $87.98 and is 5.7% above last year.
points.so_what: Higher value per order explains how revenue grew 3.3% in a week when orders fell 3.6%.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved to 15.3%, down 0.8 pp on the prior week and 1.0 pp on last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $804 of revenue, so the improvement supports the week's revenue beat.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 27 Apr 2026 was 11.3%, up 1.3 pp week on week.
points.so_what: Returns are moving the wrong way while cancellations improve, so the two quality measures are pointing in opposite directions.

points.what: New customer signups rose 21.2% to 252, up 13.0% on last year, while orders fell 3.6% in the week.
points.so_what: Customer acquisition strengthened even as order volume dipped, though signup growth of 13.0% trails order growth of 77.1% year on year.
